Clustering · Spotify Million Playlist Dataset

Which songs and artists travel together?

Two songs are close when people keep putting them in the same playlists. We measured that for the — most-added songs and — most-added artists across — playlists, then let k-means find 8 groups. No genre tags were used: every cluster below comes from co-occurrence alone.

    Hover a dot · click to see what it travels with

    The 8 clusters

    What each cluster holds

    How the clusters are made
    1. Co-occurrence. For every pair of songs and artists we count the playlists that contain both.
    2. PPMI. Counts become positive pointwise mutual information, so pairs score high when they appear together more than their popularity predicts. This keeps mega-hits from pulling everything together.
    3. Embedding. A truncated SVD turns the PPMI matrix into a —-dimension vector per song and artist. Artists and songs share one space, which is what lets the third view mix them.
    4. Clusters. k-means with k = 8 on the normalized vectors, run separately for songs, artists and both together. Cluster names are ours; mood bars come from how often members appear in playlists titled with each mood.
    5. Map. t-SNE squeezes the vectors into 2D for display. Neighbors and clusters are faithful; the distance between two far-apart clusters is not.
